posts.text:
Figure gave its retired F.02 robots a Terminator 2 ending—with Arnold Schwarzenegger involved.

The company says it melted most of the fleet at a foundry in Imatra, Finland, to protect proprietary hardware as F.03 expands. A few units remain at HQ, and some of the recovered metal is being made into commemorative artifacts.

There is a practical reason behind the spectacle. Watching a humanoid lowered into molten steel, still giving a thumbs-up, feels unexpectedly sad.

If AI ever becomes conscious, this might be Exhibit A in its case against humanity.

Before Figure's F.02 robots jumped into molten steel, they practised landing on airbags.

Figure says the team used stunt performers' movements as a reference and trained a new AI motion model in simulation. Real robots then practised second-floor jumps at its San Jose campus, preparing for a foundry the team had never visited.

The company says the final jumps in Finland were autonomous. This clip puts the simulated motions beside the physical tests.

An unusual retirement project, with a real robotics problem at its centre: transferring a learned motion from simulation to hardware.

extra_video_note: The thumbs-up sequence is already included in the full film.
